summary: Scheduled dashboard export (PDF/CSV) produces links without tracehook when executed via service-account impersonation
description:
Issue summary: Customers receive scheduled dashboard exports (PDF and CSV attachments) from the Console scheduler, but the links embedded in exported reports (View in Console / Trace links) have tracehook tokens stripped when the job is run by a service-account via impersonation. Links land on a generic 404 or a listing page without trace context, breaking runbook workflows.

Impact: Multiple enterprise customers (reported by LexiHealth) are unable to use scheduled emails to navigate to alert-linked traces or annotate dashboards. This affects on-call workflows (missed context) and compliance evidence collections that rely on tracehook parameters.

Environment: Production, us-east, scheduler v2.4, console 1.19.1, auth-service 3.2.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a dashboard with a tracehook-enabled panel (uses route param 'route_id' and customer-level aliasing).
2) Configure scheduled export (PDF and CSV) to run hourly using a service-account with impersonation scope (org-scoped).
3) Wait for job to run or trigger manually via scheduler UI.
4) Open emailed PDF/CSV and click 'View in Console' or trace links inside exports.

Expected: Links should include tracehook tokens or redirected permanent tokens so recipients land directly on the annotated dashboard/trace with preserved context.
Actual: Links arrive without tracehook query parameters or with an expired token; Console returns a generic 404 or the top-level project page.
logs:
Scheduler job ids: job-20260310-22a7, job-20260311-03f1. Example exported link from PDF: https://console.redwood.ai/orgs/lexihealth/dashboards/78?view=export (expected ?tracehook=eyJhb...)
Auth logs: impersonation token minted: sa-lexi-scheduler@lexihealth; audit entry shows 'impersonation: true' for both jobs.
Console logs (trace): 2026-03-11T03:00:12Z WARN export:sanitizer - dropped 1 query param (reason=impersonation-strip); stack=...
investigation:
Initial hypothesis: a sanitizer step in the scheduled export pipeline removes high-cardinality query params when exports are executed with service-account impersonation to avoid leaking org tokens. Evidence: 'impersonation-strip' warning in console logs. However, same sanitizer should preserve tracehook tokens by substituting with short-lived export-safe tokens (existing behaviour for user-triggered exports).
Engineer notes: Reproduced locally by running scheduler job under 'sa' token; export pipeline branches at export-service/handler.go line ~412. A related recent change merged in github.com/redwood-inference/console PR #2418 tightened query-param allowlist for impersonated jobs.
Next steps: confirm whether exporter is expected to token-swap for impersonated runs; if so, revert/disallow the overbroad sanitizer and add explicit tracehook handling. Track a fix PR and add e2e test.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Customer (LexiHealth) - Sarah Nguyen: We rely on scheduled reports during night shifts; links inside yesterday's PDF were opening to a generic page, losing incident context. Attaching example PDF.

2026-03-10 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Thanks Sarah — we've triaged and escalated. Can you confirm whether scheduled jobs run under an org service-account or a user? Also confirm whether exports triggered manually from the UI work as expected.
2026-03-11 - Customer (Sarah Nguyen): Confirmed: they run under org service-account (sa-lexi-scheduler). Manual exports include trace links correctly. Happy to provide audit logs.

2026-03-11 - Eng (Marco Ruiz): Reproduced in staging. Found console log entry 'export:sanitizer - dropped query param' for impersonated runs. Suspect PR #2418 tightened allowlist. Creating a targeted fix and unit tests.
(added linked PR github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/2471)

2026-03-12 - Support (Aisha Kapoor): Provided temporary workaround to LexiHealth to run manual exports or change scheduled job to run under an org user until fix is deployed. Customer accepted workaround but requests priority SLA.
workaround: Short-term: change scheduled job to run under a normal user account (not service-account impersonation) or switch scheduled job to call a webhook that triggers a server-side export in the customer's environment. Both options preserve tracehook tokens. Support has documented steps and shared with customer.
